The diagram above shows the function $y=f(x).$ Which of the following gives the graph of $y=-\frac{1}{2}f(x-1)?$
questions.worked_solution:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

1\. First, we perform the transformations *inside* the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches and reflections, followed by horizontal translations.

2\. Then, we perform the transformations *outside* the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches and reflections, followed by vertical translations.

To plot $y=-\frac{1}{2}f(x-1),$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=f(x).$

- Translate it by $1$ unit to the right to get the graph of $y=f(x-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250802/assets/bdb1b3bc6704af4deab77e027c5dd8f00eb929d37ddf1765866ff9d6cdbc5a7e.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}f(x-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250802/assets/ce42d16b09528a1a5ef0b2e0866081af8e5593ebdacb741be620944fd6a7dcd0.png)

- Finally, reflect the result across the $x$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\frac{1}{2}f(x-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250802/assets/640e2dd9fc8caea9d0a2b03bfdb35ad25f656e40e409e7e9778745fe16c595d9.png)
